CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old HIV-positive male presenting for follow-up of hypogonadism. Patient reports feeling well on current testosterone replacement therapy at 1 milliliter every 10 days (140 milligrams). He notes improved vigor, better sleep, and positive improvements in bloodwork. Patient reports significant improvement in cholesterol and triglyceride levels since starting testosterone in May (triglycerides decreased from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL). Red blood cell count has increased and remained stable. Patient asked about increasing testosterone dose to 175 milligrams but understands rationale for maintaining current dose due to peak testosterone levels greater than 1,500 and associated cardiovascular risks. Patient is taking finasteride 2.5 milligrams daily (half of 5 milligram pill) and cialis variably (5 milligrams on workout days, 2.5 milligrams otherwise), though reports recent shortage of cialis. Patient has been out of cialis supply.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies weight loss. Reports good energy, improved sleep, and overall feeling well. No other concerns noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV infection. History of hypogonadism. History of elevated triglycerides.

MEDICATIONS
Testosterone replacement therapy 1 milliliter every 10 days.
Finasteride 2.5 milligrams daily (half of 5 milligram tablet).
Cialis 2.5-5 milligrams daily as needed.
